case_title: Sanjai Tiwari v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.420, s.467, s.468, s.471, s.477A, s.120B; Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 s.13(1)(c)/(d) read with s.13(2)
trial_court_outcome: No verdict or sentence; trial pending, charges not framed as on date of the judgment
high_court_outcome: Section 482 application filed by respondent No.2 disposed of by directing the trial court to expedite and conclude the trial at the earliest
neutral_facts: The allegations concern corruption and related offences of cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy said to have been committed by the accused, who was one of six persons against whom a case was lodged. The matter began with a complaint made by a private individual, after which the Vigilance Department of the State of Uttar Pradesh conducted an inquiry into the accused. Following a direction by the Vigilance Department's Secretary to lodge a report, a First Information Report was registered against the accused and five others as FIR No. 02 of 2006. The FIR invoked provisions of the Indian Penal Code dealing with cheating, forgery, use of forged documents, falsification of accounts and criminal conspiracy, together with sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The Vigilance Department completed its investigation and filed a charge-sheet against the accused on 23 May 2020. The judgment does not set out the specific facts of the alleged transactions or describe the evidence collected on the merits of the charges. The FIR is stated to have been lodged on 9 January 2006, and the delay in the case is attributed to the accused by a third party; these are allegations and not findings of the court.
number_of_offences: 7 charged (IPC ss.420, 467, 468, 471, 477A, 120B; PC Act s.13(1)(c)/(d)); 0 finally upheld, as no charges had been framed
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 09.09.2020; Supreme Court: 16.12.2020
legal_representation: Not stated separately for the accused and the State; the listed counsel (including Sharan Thakur, AAG) appeared for the parties
investigation_status: FIR registered (FIR No.02/2006); charge-sheet filed 23.05.2020; charges not framed; trial pending
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Court; the appellant alleged the High Court passed the order without issuing notice to him (argument only)
appeal_history: Trial court: no verdict, trial pending. High Court: application under s.482 disposed of directing expedited trial (09.09.2020). Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court order set aside, s.482 application dismissed
prosecution_argument: State submitted that trials under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be held day to day and no exception can be taken to the High Court's order
defence_argument: Respondent No.2 had no locus standi; the High Court passed the order without notice to the appellant; the delay was not caused by the accused; the High Court's stay on the proceedings and the dismissal of the writ petition for non-appearance were not brought to the High Court's notice
legal_principle_applied: High Court may direct expedition of Prevention of Corruption Act trials, but a third party with no connection to the criminal proceeding has no locus to seek it through a public interest application
precedent_relied_upon: Janata Dal v. H.S. Chowdhary and Others (1993) 1 SCC 756
other_sentence_order: Court clarified that its observations do not affect the criminal trial; trial court may expedite the trial subject to any pending High Court orders
